reason: Narrower: the galea is the hooded upper lip of a two-lipped corolla (Pedicularis, Orobanchaceae, Lamiaceae), as rule R2821 (galea -> corolla lip). Because 'corolla' is named here, the Aconitum and orchid senses (a hooded sepal) are excluded. The position 'upper' (FLOPO_0991376) can be added under pattern 18. Truncate, conical, length and colour are qualities of the lip.

target: labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) with has position lateral (FLOPO_0991380), pattern 18
reason: A position in the series of labellum lobes. 'Side lobe' alone is a rejected bearer word because it needs its organ, and here the organ is named. This follows 'lip midlobe' and 'lip segment' -> labellum lobe (R2843, R2825). The examples (side lobes erect, incurved, falcate) are orchid lips. In two-lipped corollas (Lamiaceae, Acanthaceae) use corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) with the same position.

Narrower: the sheathing lower part of the petiole in monocots such as Araceae, palms and Zingiberales ('vaina erecta', 'narrowing gradually to apex'). PO defines leaf sheath as the lower part of a vascular leaf that more or less encases the stem, which fits, and PO gives 'vaina de la hoja' as a synonym.

Narrower: the chaffy paleae on the receptacle of a flower head, each subtending one floret. The examples are spatulate, navicular and blackish. This follows receptacular scale, receptacle scale and receptacular chaff -> flower bract (R2364, R2593, R2733). 'Chaff' is already a PO synonym of flower bract.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of palea (PO_0009038), apex region with container
reason: The apex region of an existing class, as 'glume apex' (R3732). PO has no palea apex class. Obtuse, acute, bifid and penicillate are apex qualities. Bract apex (PO_0025154) would also fit, but the rule follows the glume precedent so that both are written the same way.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of leaf sheath (PO_0020104), apex region with container
reason: The apex (mouth) region of the leaf sheath, as in Cyperaceae and Poaceae ('apex hyaline, colorless, broadly obtuse to acuminate'). PO has no leaf sheath apex class, and the region pattern expresses it.

Narrower: the leaves that subtend flowers or verticillasters within the flowering region (Lamiaceae such as Dracocephalum and Comanthosphace; Anabasis; Cuphea). The qualities 'bracteiform' and 'subsessile' fit, and PO lists hypsophyll under bract. The rule uses bract rather than inflorescence bract or flower bract because floras do not say which one is meant.

target: spikelet (PO_0009051) with bearer state pedicellate (PATO_0001438), pattern 04
reason: The pedicelled member of the sessile/pedicelled spikelet pair of Andropogoneae (reduced, neutral, staminate, aborted). PO's pedicellate spikelet classes exist only for maize (ear PO_0006348, tassel PO_0006312), so the general spikelet with the state 'pedicellate' is used. A general 'pedicellate spikelet' parent for the two maize classes would be a useful PO request, but no FLOPO class is needed.

Near-exact: PO's definition of bark (PO_0004518) says bark 'may be divided into dead outer bark and living inner bark, which consists of secondary phloem (PO:0005043)'. Granular, fibrous, cream and reddish are the qualities of the living bark seen in a cut.

target: bract margin (PO_0025011) part of involucre (PO_0009100), margin with container
reason: The margins of the bracts that make up the involucre ('margen escarioso glabro', 'conspicuous white or pinkish to purple'). An involucre is a set of bracts, so bract margin with the involucre as container is the exact reading. This follows the margin-of-a-part rule R3744.

label: fruit wing
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009084 (pericarp)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a thin, flat, membranous, papery or coriaceous extension of the pericarp (PO:0009084), projecting from the body of the fruit, as in samaras.
reason: A real, frequent structure with its own qualities: length, width, fan-shaped, papery, sericeous, spreading at an angle. Examples include Acer, Acridocarpus and other Malpighiaceae, Fraxinus, Ulmus, Combretaceae and Dioscorea. Bare 'wing' is a rejected generic word, and 'fruit winged' only gives presence. FLOPO already has seed wing (FLOPO_0986091) and anther wing (FLOPO_0986137) as precedents. Wings formed by the calyx (Dipterocarpaceae) are calyx lobes, not this class. Propose it to PO upstream.

Narrower: the axis of a spike inflorescence (PO_0030117), as 'panicle axis' -> inflorescence axis (R2685). PO lists 'inflorescence rachis' as a synonym, and the examples say 'rhachis flexuous, complanate'.
Exact: the class exists. Only the plural and the Portuguese and Spanish forms failed to ground. 'a los páreas' is a parsing fragment, not a position.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of trichome (PO_0000282), base region with container; limit to fern contexts (rhizome, stipe, frond, lamina)
reason: The examples are fern indumentum scales (Pyrrosia, Asplenium, Antrophyum): clathrate, peltate, auriculate and dentate bases. The reviewed sense split sends indumentum scales to trichome (R3675). Bare 'scale' is rejected as generic, so the rule must be limited to fern contexts. Bulb, cone and bud scales are not covered.

Narrower: the wall is the tissue of the cupule itself (Fagaceae: 'wall 4-6 mm thick, woody, fused internally'). Thickness, woodiness and hairiness of the wall are qualities of the cupule. No separate class is needed.
Narrower: a branch of a cyme inflorescence. PO_0009081 has the synonym 'inflorescence branch'. Length, stoutness and pubescence fit an axis.

target: bark (PO_0004518) as the bearer of slash qualities
reason: A slash is a cut made through the bark of a living trunk, not a structure. Its colour, smell and exudate are those of the exposed bark, mainly the inner bark. Statements should take bark (PO_0004518) as bearer, which is the safe target because a slash can also show outer layers or sapwood. Use secondary phloem when 'inner' is stated. 'slash' is already listed as a context word in the bearer limits of the rules.

target: anther theca appendage (FLOPO_0986131) in Ericaceae; connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073) in Zingiberaceae
reason: Narrower, and the class depends on the family. Most statements are Erica, where the crests are outgrowths on the back of the thecae (lacerate, ciliolate, lanceolate): an anther theca appendage. In Zingiberaceae (Zingiber, Geostachys) the anther crest is the connective extended beyond the thecae ('extends forming a beak'): a connective appendage. Bare 'crest' stays rejected.

label: bacterial leaf nodule
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0025034 (leaf)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a leaf (PO:0025034) that is a dot-like to linear swelling, usually in the lamina, housing symbiotic bacteria, as in Pavetta, Psychotria and Ardisia.
reason: A real structure with its own taxonomic qualities: dot-like, elliptic, linear, scattered, present. It is a key character in Rubiaceae (Pavetta, Psychotria) and Primulaceae (Ardisia) across African floras. Rule R0817 already says these are not root nodules (PO_0003023). FLOPO already has a comparable leaf structure, domatium (FLOPO_0986021). Propose it to PO upstream beside root nodule.

All examples are Equisetum, where the sheath is the connate whorl of leaves and the tube is its fused part below the teeth. PO has no class for it: PO leaf sheath (PO_0020104) is part of a single vascular leaf, and microphyll is obsolete. The words alone could also mean an ochrea, a sedge leaf sheath or a spathe tube, and bare 'sheath' is a rejected generic word. Revisit with an Equisetum leaf-sheath class if horsetail treatments matter.

Exact: leaf blade is a synonym of leaf lamina. Where 'secondary' is stated ('secondary veins 8-16 pairs'), secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140) is the narrower target, as in R2833. Pair counts follow pattern 03 or 14.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) part of glume (PO_0009039), with has position median (FLOPO_0991381)
reason: The median vein of a glume. PO's leaf midvein (PO_0020139) is part of a vascular leaf and does not fit a glume. Green, prominent, keeled, excurrent and mucronate are qualities of the vein. '1-3 côtes longitudinales' counts the glume's veins (pattern 03) rather than midribs.

Narrower: the putamen is the hard, lignified endocarp (the stone) of a drupe. Smooth, rugose, ridged, solid and 3 mm long are qualities of that stone wall. Where a flora means the stone together with its seed, pyrene (FLOPO_0986026) is the alternative.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of sporophyll (PO_0009026), apex region with container
reason: The apex region of the sporophyll (Lycopodiaceae, Selaginella): acuminate, acute, caudate, bristled. PO has sporophyll margin but no sporophyll apex, so the region pattern is used, as for glume apex (R3732).

target: stalk (PO_0025066) part of monocarp (FLOPO_0986046), with container
reason: In Annonaceae, the stalk of each monocarp. 'Stipe' maps to stalk in earlier rules (C264, R2829), and the monocarp class exists to serve as container. Length, thickness, clavate shape and fulvous indumentum are qualities of the stalk.

label: endoglossum
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0020075 (mericarp)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a membranous to fibrous flap growing from the inner wall of a mericarp (PO:0020075) and partly enclosing or retaining the seed, as in Gaya and related Malveae (Malvaceae).
reason: A distinct structure whose presence or absence, texture, insertion and seed retention are key characters in Malveae (Gaya, Malvastrum, Tetrasida). No PO class fits: mapping it to endocarp would turn 'endoglossum absent' into 'endocarp absent'. Keep it in FLOPO only; it is too narrow to propose to PO.

target: bract (PO_0009055) part of branch tendril (PO_0025364), with container
reason: In Cissus and other Vitaceae, a small triangular, ciliate scale on the tendril. It is a reduced bract on the tendril, which is a modified shoot. Bare 'scale' is a rejected generic word, so the bearer is bract with the tendril as container.

target: pinna (FLOPO_0985027) with has position basal (FLOPO_0991002), pattern 18
reason: A position in the series of pinnae (palms such as Euterpe; ferns such as Tectaria), as 'median pinna' (FLOPO_0996030) in config/flopo_positioned_parts.tsv. Counts of pairs, size and dissection are qualities of the pinna.

Narrower: outgrowths on the inner face of a petal, such as the paired ligules at the petal base in Bromeliaceae (Alcantarea) and the coronal scales of Caryophyllaceae ('appendages 2'). These follow 'throat appendage' -> corolline corona (R3052). Orchid petal appendages (Brachionidium) are not coronas; that context should not use the rule. Bare 'appendage' stays rejected.
